title: cfad: Characteristic Function Anomaly Detector for Financial Time Series
description: cfad is research-oriented Python software for empirical characteristic-function analysis of distributional change in financial time series. The package provides rolling ECF estimation, real-frequency distributional discrepancy scores, two-sided Page-CUSUM monitoring, parametric characteristic-function models, goodness-of-fit tools, walk-forward backtesting, bootstrap and sensitivity diagnostics, reproducible Monte Carlo validation workflows, and optional Cython acceleration. The project is designed for methodological research, benchmarking, and reproducible experimentation rather than unqualified production anomaly-detection claims.

creators.name: Ribeiro, Diogo
creators.affiliation: Faculty of Media Arts and Design, Technical University of Porto, Vila do Conde, Portugal

method: Rolling empirical characteristic functions are evaluated on real-frequency grids and summarized with normalized distributional discrepancy scores. Sequential monitoring uses standardized score sequences with a two-sided Page-CUSUM. Reproducible simulation benchmarks evaluate false-alarm behaviour, finite-window shape discrimination, null-law transportability, location/scale specificity, and comparisons with targeted and omnibus distributional summaries.
notes: Validation status: the repository preserves frozen negative confirmatory evidence as well as successful software tests. Current validation does not establish a statistically validated sequential detector or superiority over simpler moment-based shape summaries; these negative results are retained rather than tuned away after inspection.
references: Epps, T. W. and Pulley, L. B. (1983). A test for normality based on the empirical characteristic function. Biometrika 70(3), 723-726.
Page, E. S. (1954). Continuous inspection schemes. Biometrika 41(1-2), 100-115.
Cont, R. and Tankov, P. (2004). Financial Modelling with Jump Processes. Chapman & Hall/CRC.
